newsitem.title: UK: Tankers collide off French coast.
newsitem.headline: Tankers collide off French coast.

text.p: Two tankers collided in thick fog in the North Sea on Saturday and one of them was leaking unleaded petrol, British coast guards said.
No one was injured in the collision 30 miles northeast of Dover and neither ship was in danger of sinking, a coast guard spokesman said.

But the French maritime authority for the region said there was some danger that the spilled petrol might explode. "There is little danger of pollution, but there is a significant risk of an explosion due to the volatility of the spilled fuel," it said.
The tanker Bona Fulmar reported that it had been in collision with the Mexican-registered chemical tanker Teoatl, Lloyd's casualty reporting service said.

"It occurred in very dense fog. The visibility was in the region of 300 yards (metres)," Derek Smith of the Dover coast guard told Sky television. He said the Bona Fulmar had lost about 3,000 cubic metres of unleaded petrol.

Lloyd's said the Bona Fulmar sustained a large hole, three metres high and four metres wide (nearly 10 by 13 feet), some of it below the waterline. The tanker's crew were changing ballast to try to stop the leak.
Smith said the collision occurred in French waters and French officials were coordinating the rescue with British assistance. A tugboat was on the scene helping.

"Teoatl has assessed damage and is proceeding to Rotterdam under her own power," Lloyd's said. "There are considerable fumes in the area and vessels in transit are being advised by broadcast to proceed with great caution."
